summary: Five-lens review of the balanced-rounds statistical design (proof, independent numerical attack, enumeration code, decision and claims, product contract), then adversarial verification of each finding

sound.checked_and_sound: (1) The AM-GM step is correct: every factor is at least 1-q >= 1/2, the expectation of the round product factorises under within-round independence, the bound holds for each fixed q and therefore for the equal mixture of full products; I found no error in PROOF steps 1 to 9 under their stated assumptions. (2) Needed are joint independence of cells within a round, independence of each round from earlier rounds, and each round's own suite mean obeying the null; identical cell laws across rounds are sufficient but not necessary, and an average-over-rounds null is not enough (finding 1, with exact counterexamples). (3) Ville is applied correctly at round ends (W_0=1, inclusive threshold 40, a cap only shrinks the event) and first-stop keeps both directional bounds because each declared verdict is a subset of its own crossing event. (4) At round ends the product commutes, so there is no dependence on cell order or on any schedule; the only residual dependence is on round order, and only when laws are not stationary. (5) A weighted suite mean works if cell stakes are proportional to weights (lam_c = lam*w_c/w_max gives a bound base of 1 + lam*(Delta_w+delta)/(N*w_max)), so PROOF.md:17 is slightly too strong: cell-dependent stakes retarget the null rather than break validity. Repeating cell c k_c times per round is valid only for the k-weighted mean; against the unweighted null it fails (nine +1 cells run twice and eleven -1 cells once give round factors 5.13 and 2.61), so every round must hold every cell exactly once. (6) The mid-round counterexample is correct: wealth 151874368379777/5642219814912 = 26.92 at pair 8 and 316547748620285/7522959753216 = 42.08 at pair 9, complete-round PASS factors 0.465 and 0.036, BLOCK factors 0.582 and 0.085; decide gives PASS at pair 9 with pairwise looks and INCONCLUSIVE at 400 by rounds, and a terminal partial round is indeed an unprotected look. (7) Scoring an errored pair as -1 for PASS and +1 for BLOCK keeps each test valid: each wealth is monotone in d, so the scored path is pointwise at most the path under any fill-in of the errored pairs, the crossing event shrinks whatever causes the errors, and both tests still cannot cross together; the errored pair must stay in its round as a factor, never be dropped or replaced. Enumeration check: an independently written absorbing recursion over rounds equalled balanced.enumerate_balanced exactly (N=5, cap 100, heterogeneous three-support laws; all probabilities and expected pairs equal as fractions), and the stationary even law at N=20 reproduced 0.009034 / 0.004849. I did not run run_all.py or s1c_study.py and wrote nothing in the repository; check scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay--claude-spares-spare-8K9guD/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad/ (chk2.py, chk3.py).

The round-end claim survived the numerical attack: no configuration exceeded alpha/2 anywhere. I wrote an independent evaluator (state = counts of -1 and +1, exact integer verdict regions checked three ways on 158,840 states, Fractions for probabilities) and it agreed with balanced.enumerate_laws as exact Fractions on 60 of 60 random small configurations (N in {2,3,4,5,8}, alpha in {1/20,1/5,1/2,4/5}, general, no-plus and no-zero laws, deterministic cells included), on 7 of 7 full 400-pair two-point cases, and with decide_rounds on 200 of 200 random streams. Boundary search (suite mean exactly -1/10, general three-support laws on a 1/1000 lattice, random restarts with extreme, bimodal, one-hot, homogeneous and uniform starts, then local search; one-sided crossing probability, winners re-evaluated exactly): 92,004 evaluations, about 2,200 to 3,900 per N-direction-alpha setting. Maxima found against the limit: alpha=1/20 (80-pair horizon) 0.012959 vs 0.025; alpha=1/5 (48 pairs) 0.051988 vs 0.1; alpha=1/2 (30 pairs) 0.149162 vs 0.25; the optimum always drifted to near-homogeneous cells at mean -delta, as AM-GM predicts. Just inside each null (mean shifted by 0.001 and 0.01 toward the null): 130,555 further evaluations, every maximum below its boundary counterpart (for example 0.012636 and 0.010920 at alpha=1/20). A hand-built battery of 837 exact configurations with deterministic +1 and -1 cells and strongly heterogeneous means peaked at 0.012658 (alpha=1/20), 0.051081 (alpha=1/5) and 0.159468 (alpha=1/2). At long horizons the bound is approached but not crossed: alpha=1/20, cap 400, homogeneous laws give at most 0.021555 (N=1) and 0.019676 (N=2); alpha=1/2 over 400 pairs gives at most 0.2312 (N=1) and 0.2053 (N=2) against 0.25. PASS and BLOCK wealth never both reach 2/alpha at any state with n<=400 for alpha in {1/2,1/5,1/20,1/100,1/1000} (exhaustive over all 80,600 (n,m) rows per alpha), and ERROR mass was 0 in every run. Mid-round looks do fail: I reproduced the spike's N=20 case exactly (pairwise looks PASS with probability 1 at pair 9, wealth 316547748620285/7522959753216; round-end looks INCONCLUSIVE with probability 1), found a smaller one at N=19 (eight deterministic +1 cells then eleven cells (19/20,0,1/20): pairwise false PASS 0.0511, round-end 2.5e-7), a stochastic N=20 case (0.3874 pairwise; 0.3487 with only one extra look per round after cell 10), and probability-1 cases at N=10 (alpha=1/2) and N=15 (alpha=1/5); a search of 13,698 configurations with N<=10 at alpha in {1/2,1/5,1/20} found no pairwise-look violation, consistent with N=20 being the smallest deterministic case at alpha=1/20. The ADR draft's fixed-per-cell seed rule already covers the across-round stationarity assumption, so I raise no finding on it. Nothing in the repository was created or changed; reviewer scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay--claude-spares-spare-8K9guD/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad (ev.py, cmp.py, search.py, long.py, extra.py, dep.py, mid.py).

The carry bound in PROOF.md items 13-14 holds: width = bit_length(final_scale)+1 so the base exceeds twice the final denominator, every digit and the total alive mass at step n are at most the running scale, which never exceeds final_scale, and the nine folds cover 512 digits against at most 401 (balanced.py lines 116-117, 152-169). I wrote a separate plain dict-of-(minus,plus)-counts DP with its own integer wealth test (no spike imports) and compared exact fractions against results.json: all 23 Table A rows match on PASS, BLOCK, INCONCLUSIVE, ERROR and expected pairs (for example N=5 even 0.012263126 / 0.006035934, N=10 mixed 0.007213118 / 0.008678212, N=20 concentrated-3 0.000089451 / 2.79e-9). Five Table C rows match in both columns, including 0.50->0.50 independent N=20 (0.519844 / 306.319 balanced, 0.537656 / 297.677 sampled) and 0.95->0.75 intermediate N=20 (0.977056 / 177.997); all six heterogeneous N=20 rows match in both columns (for example concentrated-minus-05 independent 0.295163 / 354.137 versus 0.341903 / 339.929). All seven Table D rows match; the underlying pair floors are 79 (all-zero PASS), 9 (all +1 PASS) and 13 (all -1 BLOCK), so the claim that no N in 1..400 is excluded by the all-zero floor is correct. The six search-maximum rows also match exactly. A differential test of enumerate_laws against my DP on 300 random position-dependent law sequences (mixed denominators up to 9973, deterministic, no-plus and no-zero cells, varied batch sizes, 251 with absorption) and six random heterogeneous full-cap grids (N=3,7,20,33,150,201) gave zero mismatches. Table B's method is right: laws are indexed by the scheduled cell per pair and absorbed only at multiples of 10; I recomputed 46 conditional rows (own DP, own reimplementation of cell_index, keys reproduced) including each law's maximum rows, all exact. The maxima of 1.000000 occur only for N=10 concentrated-1 and N=20 concentrated-2, where the regressing cells have P(-1)=1 and all others are deterministic zero, so conditional on a schedule the stream is deterministic and the error is 0 or 1 depending on whether the hash under- or over-draws those cells early (4 PASS and 5 BLOCK of 500 keys at N=10; 7 and 2 at N=20); the largest non-degenerate conditional error is 0.388, and no 500-key mean exceeds 0.014. decide_rounds agrees with an independent count-based verdict and stopping pair on 1,500 random streams for N in {1,2,5,7,20,33,150,201,400}, looks only at multiples of N, uses cap N*floor(400/N), and raises ValueError for a partial round, a short inconclusive stream and N > cap. In test_s1c.py I found no test that strictly cannot fail; the weak ones are the digit-sum test (unit coefficients only, so it never approaches the carry bound), the first loop of test_grid_and_search_contracts (repeats an assertion already inside boundary_cases), and the two comparisons with S1 characteristics, which share make_boundary, though test_exhaustive_paths does tie the packed path to the rational decide. As a side result, a feasible substitute for the infeasible fourth heterogeneous scenario (four 0.99 cells dropping to 0, mean -0.198, independent arms) gives balanced BLOCK 0.8222 at 262.1 expected pairs against sampled-unconditional 0.7993 at 239.4.

Numbers: I recomputed every figure in RESULTS.md's Conclusions and CODEX_REPORT.md from results.json and all match (largest Table A error 1.247230% at N=5 mixed BLOCK; search maximum 1.595637%; N=10/20/50 mean changes 0 / -0.004441 / -0.012222 with ranges to -0.017813 and -0.049406; cost +7.520 and +24.913 pairs with the stated ranges; floors; the Table E wealths; 23 A rows, 6,000 search rows, 11,500 B rows, 108 C rows); the only mismatch is cosmetic (CODEX_REPORT says 7 files formatted, RESULTS says 8). The proof is sound as written: each factor is at least 1-q > 0, AM-GM gives a per-round expectation of at most (1+lam(Delta+delta))^N <= 1 under the null and symmetrically for BLOCK, the mixture and Ville steps are one line each, and the independence it needs is honestly marked ASSUMED. The enumeration is sound: my independently written DP reproduces the spike's exact values (0.80->0.80 independent N=50: 0.759039 / 271.352; even law at N=5 and N=10; the sampled reference 0.790628 / 241.380) and the spike's code reproduces its own heterogeneous row. (a) The per-manifest argument for balanced is stronger than the '100%' headline suggests: the 100% rows are degenerate deterministic laws, but for the non-degenerate half-improving and mixed laws 8 to 16 percent of the 500 frozen schedules exceed 2.5% at every N from 5 to 100 (for example 82 of 500 at N=20 half-improving BLOCK, 74 of 500 at N=100), so sampled cannot carry a per-manifest claim and is rightly rejected as a fallback. (b) The stated cost at N=20/50 is correct, and the missing heterogeneous true-regression rows favour balanced by up to 5 points of BLOCK power. (c) Nothing I computed reverses 'balanced'; what changes is the cap rule and the usable range: as specified it is supported to about 100 cells (5 to 6 points and about 54 extra pairs at N=100), and for 100 to 400 cells only if the cap is a whole number of rounds rounded up or a larger cap is registered, and above 400 a larger cap is the only route. Sentence verdicts: 'at most 2.5 percent for the manifest as written' is true only with the independence, complete-round and no-missing-pair conditions; 'cannot PASS before 80 pairs' is false (true floor for a never-differing candidate is ceil(79/N)*N, and no-change candidates with noise pass earlier 5 to 25 percent of the time); '4 rounds with 20 cells' is the never-differing case, with one round the true minimum and 5 to 13 rounds typical; 'at most about 5 points' is true for N <= 50 only (4.94 and 4.96 maxima). The brief's defect was handled honestly (disclosed in three files, six feasible rows computed, nothing clipped or invented) and the six rows do answer the within-margin question: balanced passes less often in five of six, by 0.08 to 4.96 points, though the Conclusions do not say so. Process disclosure: I wrote nothing in the repository and did not run run_all.py or s1c_study.py; two scratch scripts live in the session scratchpad; one of my computations overran the 4-minute guide and I stopped it with `pkill -f "python -B -"`, a pattern broad enough to have also terminated other Python processes started with `-B -c` or `-B -` at that moment (a process list taken afterwards showed no run_all job, so I cannot confirm whether the regeneration job or a sibling reviewer was affected); the large-grid and worst-case figures are from my float DP, not exact rationals.

Proof and code: I re-derived the round step (each factor is linear in d with expectation at least 1 - q, so the round expectation factorises under independence, or under fixed conditional means taken cell by cell, and AM-GM bounds it by 1 on the null) and found no error; importing the spike read-only I reproduced Table A (N=20 even 0.009034434 / 0.004849156, N=5 even 0.012263126 / 0.006035934), all seven Table D floors, and the mid-round counterexample (PASS at pair 9, INCONCLUSIVE at round ends); no bug found in balanced.py. The reference silently ignores complete rounds after a decisive one and beyond the cap (20 all-zero rounds return PASS at 80; 25 supplied rounds are read to 400), which is a duty of the product gate, not a defect of the spike. (1) Rounds as stages: yes, the v1 pattern in /Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/src/arci/runner.py lines 1568-1593 (submit a stage, wait for all of it, store, decide, break on PASS, BLOCK or ERROR) maps directly onto rounds if the last pair_id component, which gate.py:329 and runner.py:1575 parse as the pair index, is the round number and each cell plays the part of a v1 condition; order and parallelism inside a round are free because rational products commute and nothing is evaluated mid-round, provided concurrency does not couple outcomes (shared rate limits or timeouts scored FAIL, shared caches) and nothing cancels part of a round. The gate must verify: the suite manifest seal, and that experiment_id equals the digest it recomputes from the rule and grid; unique trial ids, each matching its rebuilt TrialSpec (spec_sha256, seed, arm, task_id, condition_id); that the stored set is exactly rounds 1 to r with every cell and both arms; that recomputed wealth is undecided at every round end before r and decisive at r, or r is the registered last round; no trial of round r+1; valid trial seals. (2) Seeds: take the first 8 bytes of SHA-256(domain tag, 32-byte suite key, round as 8 bytes big-endian, SHA-256 of the canonical cell identity), masked to 63 bits (53 if the HTML report reads seeds as JavaScript numbers), the same for both arms, with the key a SHA-256 over canonical ASCII JSON holding rationals as strings; use no random module, no hash() and no floats, and freeze golden vectors in CI across Python versions and both operating systems; what the seed may influence is finding 1. (3) ERROR is finding 2: worst-case scoring with a registered maximum is valid and should be the default, void is valid per run only. (4) Hard invariants: evaluate at the round end, with ERROR above BLOCK above a statistical PASS as in v1; an immediate stop would leave a partial round that the store check must reject and a stopping point that depends on completion order. The override sits outside the 2.5 percent false-BLOCK claim: an unchanged candidate whose trials break a hard invariant 1 percent of the time is blocked with probability 0.72 by 126 pairs and 0.98 by 400, so the report must show baseline hard violations beside the candidate's. (5) Grid limits and planning are finding 3; per cell the report should show rounds completed, successes per arm, counts of d = -1, 0, +1, errored pairs and how they were scored, hard violations per arm and faults declared against fired, all labelled descriptive with n equal to the number of rounds, beside a per-round table of both wealths against the threshold 40. (6) TrialSpec (src/arci/schema.py lines 471-499): interval_method cannot name the betting rule and defaults to 'clopper_pearson', and looks=() means one look at n_per_arm in v1, so a suite trial's spec would state the v1 rule; alpha and delta are floats (0.1 is not 1/10), so they can only be informational mirrors of the rational rule. The grid, round count, stakes, ERROR policy and the check function are not TrialSpec fields, so their binding rests entirely on experiment_id, which works only if the gate recomputes that digest from the manifest content; experiment_id is also a directory name (storage.py:12), and cell identity should be read from the envelope's task_id and condition_id, never parsed out of pair_id, because ids may contain ':'.

surviving.title: Stationarity is load-bearing: with a different seed per (round, cell) the bound is not 'for every manifest, over outcome randomness only'
surviving.claim: The round-end supermartingale needs EVERY round's suite mean to obey the null; PROOF step 1 gets this by assuming each cell's law is identical in every round. A manifest that gives each (round, cell) its own seed, as v1 does, fixes a different scenario per round, so conditional on the manifest the laws are not stationary, and when only the average over rounds sits on the margin the process is not a supermartingale. The guarantee then holds only on average over the scenario-seed draw, which is the same kind of averaged guarantee S1b rejected for sampled cells.
surviving.recommendation: ADR 0011 should (a) state the null per round: PASS rejects 'every round's suite mean <= -delta', BLOCK the mirror; (b) choose and state the seed rule. Either one scenario seed per cell held across all rounds with fresh, uncached model randomness per round (a true conditional-per-manifest guarantee whose estimand is the N fixed scenarios), or a distinct seed per (round, cell) with scenario seeds assumed to be i.i.d. draws per cell exactly as v1 assumes; in the second case the release wording becomes 'no schedule randomness; holds for every grid and cell order, on average over scenario seeds', not 'every manifest, outcome randomness only'. (c) Show per-round suite means in the report as a disclosed (not detected) drift indicator, since provider drift during a run has the same effect. (d) Carry the non-stationary rows above into the phase-1 tests.
surviving.evidence: Proof of the exact condition: E[B_r | F_{r-1}] = prod_c(1+lam(Delta_{r,c}+delta)) <= (1+lam(mean_c Delta_{r,c}+delta))^N, which is <= 1 iff round r's own suite mean <= -delta (and exceeds 1 when cells are equal and that mean is above -delta). Counterexamples, exact, via balanced.enumerate_laws with balanced_plan(20): N=20, 20 rounds, independent across cells and rounds, every cell P(-1)=p_r, P(0)=1-p_r, mean of p_r exactly 1/10 (so the manifest-wide mean and every cell's time average are exactly -delta). p=0 for 10 rounds then 1/5: false PASS 1.000000 (stops at pair 80). Reversed: false BLOCK 0.847500. Linear 0 -> 0.2: false PASS 0.771708. Linear 0.05 -> 0.15: false PASS 0.118321; reversed: false BLOCK 0.055510. Linear 0.08 -> 0.12: false PASS 0.025056 (already above 1/40). Stationary p=0.1: 0.009034 / 0.004849 (matches RESULTS Table A). The mid-round counterexample is this same failure with N=1. Nothing in the spike measures it: enumerate_balanced repeats `list(laws) * rounds` (balanced.py:94-96), so every table uses stationary laws. Sources: PROOF.md:5-7 ('Cell laws are fixed across rounds... The theorem conditions on the manifest'), PROOF.md:47-50 (step 10 names the weaker per-round condition but 'does not establish those assumptions'); RESULTS.md:227 and :233 ('conditional-per-manifest guarantee'); brief line 33; src/arci/schedule.py:53 (seed = base_seed + j*n_per_arm + i, distinct per repetition); docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:11-16 (same TrialSpec gives identical results; RNGs derived from the spec seed), so for a seeded deterministic agent each (round, cell) outcome is a constant fixed by the manifest. v1 comparison: docs/STATISTICS.md:8 assumes 'Trials are independent across trial ids' and its binomial intervals implicitly treat the seed-indexed repetitions of a condition as identically distributed; v1 never claims a per-manifest guarantee, its fixed-N verdict depends on counts only (order-free), and only its few prefix looks are order-sensitive. The balanced gate is order-sensitive at up to 400/N looks.

surviving.title: Independence across cells and rounds must be enforced by seed derivation; a round-level seed or cross-round replay gives 30 to 67 percent error with every marginal on the margin
surviving.claim: The proof factorises a product of N expectations, so it needs joint independence across (round, cell), not just the right mean per pair. The spike states this as an assumption and a caller contract but gives no product requirement that makes it true. Positive dependence among the cells of one round, or repeating a round's random outcomes in later rounds, breaks the bound even when every cell law and every round mean is exactly stationary and on the margin.
surviving.recommendation: Whichever seed rule finding 1 selects: no two cells of one round may share a seed (no round-level seed), the two arms of one pair may; seeds are derived by hash from (schedule key, round, cell) and the gate checks them against the schedule as v1 does. If a seed is reused for a cell across rounds, a gate run must not serve a later round from a recording or response cache of an earlier one. State plainly that a shared-infrastructure burst hitting many cells of one round (scored FAIL, not ERROR) is outside the guarantee, the same limitation as v1's 'independent across trial ids'. Add the two cases above to the phase-1 tests as known-failure demonstrations.
surviving.corrected_claim:
The balanced-round proof needs joint independence of the paired differences across (round, cell). The spike states this only as an assumption and caller contract and gives no product requirement for it. The bound is fragile to positive dependence even when every cell marginal is stationary and on the margin. Exact, N=20, 20 rounds, P(-1)=1/10 per cell: independent 0.009034 false PASS / 0.004849 false BLOCK; cells sharing a draw in pairs 0.0809 / 0.0487; whole round sharing one draw 0.672777 / 0.318217; round 1 replayed in rounds 2 to 20 0.391747 / 0.323073.

Severity is a must-state requirement and disclosed limit, not a design change:

1. Carry S1-review decision 4 (trial seeds by SHA-256 from schedule key and pair index) over to the balanced design as (schedule key, round, cell), with the two arms of a pair sharing a seed.
2. Keep v1's gate check of seed and `spec_sha256` against the schedule. It already excludes ARCI's own REPLAY mode from gate runs.
3. State that seeds do not by themselves create independence. Fresh processes and reset state per trial are required, and no response cache or recording may serve one trial from another.
4. Disclose that external caches and shared-infrastructure bursts scored FAIL are outside the guarantee, as with v1's "independent across trial ids".
5. Add the dependence cases as known-failure demonstrations in phase-1 tests.
surviving.evidence: Exact, N=20, 20 rounds, every cell marginally P(-1)=1/10, P(0)=9/10 (independent case: 0.009034 false PASS, 0.004849 false BLOCK). (i) Cells of a round share one draw (round is all 0 w.p. 0.9, all -1 w.p. 0.1; rounds independent), computed by a count DP over rounds with suite_stats.count_wealth/classify: false PASS 0.672777, false BLOCK 0.318217. (ii) Round 1 drawn independently, rounds 2 to 20 replay it: false PASS 0.391747, false BLOCK 0.323073. Analytic check of the mechanism: N=2 comonotone +/-1 cells with mean -delta give E[B] = 1 + lam^2*Var(d) = 1 + (5/9)^2 * 0.99 = 1.3056 at q=1/2, so the round factor has expectation above 1. Sources: PROOF.md:8-11 (step 2: 'does not license shared random outcomes across cells or rounds'), PROOF.md:47-51; RESULTS.md:237; balanced.py:53-54 ('Cell identity and law independence are caller contracts, not detectable from differences alone'); docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:44 and :53-55 (record/replay tool modes exist in the product); S1-review.md decision 4 leaves trial-seed derivation to the design record.

surviving.title: Within-round independence has no slack: a 2% rate of round-wide common shocks, or one single-arm outage round, breaks the 2.5% bound
surviving.claim: The round-end guarantee holds only if the N differences inside a round are independent; the spike marks this ASSUMED and gives no sensitivity. Because a balanced round is also a block of wall-clock time, one transient incident that hits one arm across a round produces exactly the dependence the AM-GM step cannot absorb, and at N>=20 a single such round decides the verdict by itself. The spike's 'balanced only' recommendation and the ADR's 'order and parallelism inside a stage are free' leave the runner requirement that protects against this unstated.
surviving.recommendation: Keep the theorem but state its dependence limit with these numbers. In the ADR: (a) name common-mode failure (provider incident, rate limiting under in-round parallelism, one arm's endpoint down) as a violation of item 6, not only caches; (b) decide how provider or transport failures of one arm are classified: as errored pairs under item 9 (scored against both tests) rather than FAIL, or disclose that they are scored as outcomes; (c) report per-round, per-arm success rates beside the verdict so a one-round collapse is visible; (d) do not describe the guarantee as holding 'for every manifest' without the independence clause attached to the same sentence.
surviving.evidence: Own evaluator (float DP, exact integer boundaries; rho=0 rows reproduce the exact values 0.013966/0.016072 and the spike's Table C 0.928342 and 0.999462). Marginal law of every cell held exactly on the margin (mean -1/10 every round); with probability rho a round is a 'common' round where all N cells share one draw. Cap 400, alpha=1/20. N=20, law (.55,0,.45): rho=0 -> PASS/BLOCK crossing 0.0082/0.0115; rho=0.02 -> 0.0412/0.0449; rho=0.05 -> 0.0906/0.0967; rho=0.25 -> 0.351/0.385. N=20, law (.1,.9,0): rho=0.02 -> BLOCK 0.0348; N=20, law (.15,.80,.05): rho=0.02 -> BLOCK 0.0376. N=5 crosses 2.5% at rho=0.05 (0.0303/0.0312 for the two-point law). One-round outage, N=20, independent arms: baseline 0.95 vs candidate 0.75 (true difference -0.20) gives BLOCK 0.9283 normally; if the baseline arm fails every cell in round 1 only, PASS=0.9998; in round 2 only, PASS=0.7615. Identical arms at 0.95 give PASS 0.9995 normally; candidate arm down in round 1 only gives BLOCK=1.0000, round 2 only BLOCK=0.9124. Mechanism: 20 pairs of d=-1 multiply BLOCK wealth by (53/44)^20=41 and (31/22)^20=952, mixture about 497 >= 40 (Table D 'earliest BLOCK 20'). Files: PROOF.md step 1 (ASSUMED) and line 49 ('does not establish those assumptions for a real provider'); adr-0011-draft.md line 62 (names only fresh processes and caches) and item 8 ('Order and parallelism inside a stage are free'); docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md line 8 (agent crash, timeout, budget exhaustion = FAIL, so a provider incident is scored as an outcome, not an ERROR); PLAN.md line 224 (baseline and candidate are two different hosted models, so an incident can hit one arm only).

surviving.title: The reported worst case (1.596%, '1.6%' in the ADR draft) is not the worst: the proof's own equality case and small grids reach 1.67% to 2.16%
surviving.claim: The adversarial search covers only loss-zero and loss-win random partitions and N in {5,10,20}; it misses homogeneous laws (all cells at mean -delta, the equality case named in PROOF step 9) and general three-point laws, which beat every searched maximum, and it omits N<5 where the error is closest to the limit. No value exceeds 2.5%, so the guarantee stands, but the published margin is overstated.
surviving.recommendation: Replace '1.6%' with a statement tied to grid size, for example: largest error found on the margin 2.16% at N=1, 1.97% at N=2, 1.67% at N=5, 1.42% at N=10, 1.15% at N=20, all under the 2.5% limit, proved for all laws. Add the homogeneous two-point and three-point laws to Table A and to the phase 1 tests as the tightest known cases, and say the margin shrinks further if max_rounds is raised above 400 pairs (at alpha=1/2, where the cap does not bind, I measured 0.2312 against a 0.25 limit).
surviving.evidence: Exact values from balanced.enumerate_balanced at cap 400 (matched by my independent evaluator to 9 decimals, and as exact Fractions for the two-point law at N=1,2,3,4,5,10,20). N=5: law (3/10,1/2,1/5) PASS=0.016236681 vs spike search max 0.013858709; law (9/20,1/5,7/20) BLOCK=0.016672719 vs 0.015956374. N=10: law (9/20,1/5,7/20) PASS=0.012991689, BLOCK=0.014153883 vs search maxima 0.009302253 / 0.008937202 (58% higher on BLOCK).
